subject: SIG: audit trail extraction, tenant-level access & retention options
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, May 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: audit log questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Northbridge's InfoSec team is finishing up our SIG and had a few follow-ups specific to audit logging and monitoring. Can you confirm the following for hosted customers?

- Default retention period for event/audit logs (ingest + control plane).
- Supported export mechanisms (S3 exports, streaming, API) and whether exports can be scoped to a single customer/tenant.
- Whether customers can be given read-only access to their tenant's logs (or a continuously updated export).
- Evidence: a sample anonymized event log we can include with our SIG, and any documentation that describes tamper-evidence/immutability.

We need this by EOD Thursday to stay on our procurement timeline. Appreciate any specifics and an example export if possible.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Information Security
Northbridge Health

(Referenced: SIG section 6.3 - Monitoring & Audit Trails)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log questions

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary answers up front, full details below and attached samples: audit_log_schema_v2.csv (field map) and sample_event_log_anonymized.jsonl (sanitized events).

- Default retention (hosted): 90 days for full event payloads; 1 year for metadata indexes.
- Exports: daily S3 export (customer-scoped prefix + optional presigned URL delivery), on-demand CSV/JSON export via Console/API, and Kafka-compatible streaming for Dedicated/Private customers. Exports are scoped to tenant IDs; we never mix tenant data.
- Customer access: We can provision read-only Console views for tenant admins. For automated delivery, we can set up a dedicated S3 bucket with a cross-account role or provide presigned URLs to exported files on a scheduled cadence.
- Tamper-evidence: logs are append-only in the ingestion pipeline; we emit SHA256 checksums per file and retain an immutable index. For SIG purposes we provide an evidentiary package (redaction_policy_summary.pdf, export checksums).

Vivek — can you confirm the retention SLA language and whether we can offer a 365-day retention for BH/enterprise tenants on a paid add-on? Also note the recommended redaction guidance for PHI in the attached summary.

Alicia — if this looks good I can open a DocuSign for the export/data handling addendum (we have a standard template) and spin up a temporary sample export to share.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, May 10, 2026 at 11:36 AM -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log questions

Hi all,

Detail from the platform side:

1) Retention
- Hosted (default): 90 days for full event bodies (payloads), 12 months for indexed metadata (timestamps, tenant_id, event_type).
- Dedicated/Private: configurable per contract; we can commit to 365 days for enterprise plans (addendum required).

2) Export & streaming
- Scheduled exports: nightly job writes tenant-scoped files to our S3 export bucket under <tenant-id>/YYYYMMDD/, files are gzipped JSONL. We publish a SHA256 manifest for each day.
- On-demand: Console/API export endpoint that returns a presigned S3 URL (expires configurable).
- Streaming: for Dedicated customers we can push events to a customer-managed Kafka topic or Kinesis stream; this supports near-real-time sinks.

3) Tenant access & isolation
- Tenants cannot view other tenants' data; RBAC enforces tenant-level scoping.
- For hosted customers who want continuous access, we usually set up a dedicated S3 export and grant read-only cross-account role (least privilege).

4) Tamper evidence & chain of custody
- Files are append-only once written; manifests include file-level SHA256 and a signed manifest entry (internal KMS key).
- For formal audits we provide the manifest + checksum bundle and a short audit-note that explains ingestion window and pipeline worker IDs.

5) PII/PHI redaction
- We provide field-level redaction rules and can run an anonymization job for customer samples. See redaction_policy_summary.pdf attached.

6) Evidence for SIG
- Attached: sample_event_log_anonymized.jsonl (sanitized, 100 events) and audit_log_schema_v2.csv (field descriptions).
- For SOC 2 submission: we can generate a signed checksum bundle and an engineer-signed note describing the retention pipeline (we usually include this in our SIG evidence pack).

Jonas — if we can also generate a short exported sample that includes the manifest + signed bundle, please create a ticket and mark SEC-839.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

This is helpful, thank you. A couple follow-ups from our compliance team:

- For the signed manifest: can Redwood provide a signed timestamp for daily manifests (we use that to demonstrate immutability in our SIG package)?
- For continuous access: we prefer a daily S3 export into our own bucket (cross-account) rather than presigned URLs. Is that standard, and how long does provisioning take?
- For the sample event log: can you provide one with authentication events and model inference events (masked inputs) — those are the ones our reviewers care about most.

If you can confirm provisioning timeline and provide the slightly expanded sample we can close the SIG item. We can sign the export addendum once we have the DocuSign link.
